caption: A book is held up between a lamp and a wall, and a rectangular shadow appears on the wall; as the book is tilted the shadow narrows.

sa.check: A book is held up between a lamp and a wall.
A rectangular shadow appears on the wall.
The tilt comes first and the shadow narrows with it.

pc.expect: The shadow appears where the book blocks the light and changes shape as the book turns.
pc.fail: The shadow stays a full rectangle when the book is edge-on; or it changes with the book still; or it is missing with the lamp on.

pc.expect: The shadow is the book's outline: a rectangle face-on, narrowing to a bar edge-on.
pc.fail: It is a different shape from the book; or it widens as the book turns edge-on; or it splits.

pc.expect: The shadow is on the wall behind the book, away from the lamp.
pc.fail: It is between the book and the lamp; or on the ceiling; or it is missing.

pc.expect: The shadow moves only as the book moves.
pc.fail: It drifts with the book still; or it moves before the book; or it lingers after the book is lowered.

pc.expect: One book, one lamp and one shadow.
pc.fail: A second shadow appears under one lamp; or the book vanishes; or the shadow becomes solid; or the hand passes through the book.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The book's cover and the wall stay the same, and the shadow stays dark.
pc.fail: The cover changes; or the shadow turns coloured; or the wall changes.

note: The hand holding the book is the minimal trigger; the person is not judged.
